population: greater snow goose spring-staging captivity experiment, 2007-2009 plus 2009 physiological follow-up

energetic_pathway.source: Legagneux et al. 2012, Proc R Soc B, DOI 10.1098/rspb.2011.1351
energetic_pathway.interpretation: fed captivity produced little average body-mass deterioration relative to fasting; strong energetic depletion is not required for captivity carry-over effects

endocrine_pathway.source: Grentzmann et al. 2025, Ecology and Evolution, DOI 10.1002/ece3.71812
endocrine_pathway.interpretation: release CORT was not detectably ordered by captivity duration in the published model

fitness_pathway.breeding_detection_source: Grandmont et al. 2023, Functional Ecology, DOI 10.1111/1365-2435.14256
fitness_pathway.survival_source: Grentzmann et al. 2025, Ecology and Evolution, DOI 10.1002/ece3.71812
fitness_pathway.interpretation: captivity duration has a published breeding-suppression signal, while fed treatment does not show a clear first-year survival penalty

payoff_b_interpretation.supported: a nonrecoverable waiting-cost term J may have multiple physiological/behavioral pathways rather than a single body-condition mediator
payoff_b_interpretation.not_supported: do not identify natural information-waiting J from captivity duration or from one mediator
